sentences.text: Rule seven is about one question: is there a risk of collision?
And it starts with a powerful sentence: if there’s any doubt, the risk shall be deemed to exist.
So how do you judge it?
You’re the boat at the bottom, heading up the page, and another boat is crossing from your right.
Each dashed line is a bearing taken a minute or so apart.
See how the lines stay parallel?
The bearing isn’t changing, while the distance shrinks.
That’s the classic sign of a collision course.
You can do this with your eyes, too.
Line the other boat up with a stanchion or a corner of your windshield.
If it stays in that spot while it gets bigger, you’re on a collision course.
One warning: with a very large ship, a tow, or anything very close, risk can exist even when the bearing is changing.
